a:r.a:t: Nucleotide Positions in tRNAs That Are Recognized by Aminoacyl-tRNA Synthetases:

p:cNvPr.descr: Two diagrams show the positions on tRNA which are recognized by aminoacyl-tRNA synthetases. The first diagram shows this with simple dots; the other is a 3-D model. (a) A model of tRNA that shows bulges and "ladders." The tRNA backbone itself is light green; the nucleotide bonds, which resemble rungs on a ladder, are blue. In the middle of the tRNA there is an open space where the strands diverge to form the arms, so there are no nucleotide bonds here. There are dots along the green backbone which represent nucleotide positions. The amino acid arm is at the top, where the two strands begin. The 5' strand is on the left and the 3' strand is on the right. The 3' strand is slightly longer than the 5' strand, so it begins a bit higher. This region contains 3 purple dots which can bond to an amino acid. If we continue downward, the 5' strand begins on the left. On the amino acid arm, there are 7 nucleotide bonds (blue). The color of the dot listed on the 3' strand is the same color of the dot across from it on the 5' strand. The order of dot colors on the 3' strand is as follows: blue, blue, orange, blue, black, black, black, black. This ends the amino acid arm. The strands now diverge to form the D arm on the left and the T psi C arm on the right. The 3' strand curves right and begins the T psi C arm, which has a large bulge at the end with no bonds. There are still dots representing nucleotide positions. The T psi C arm with bonds has the following dot colors: black, black, black, black, purple. The bulge has no bonds inside it, but has these colors: orange, orange, purple, black, purple, purple, purple. To the lower right of the T psi C arm, there is a green dotted extension labeled "extra arm." There are no nucleotides or bonds here. Below this extra arm, pointing down, is the anticodon arm. Like the T psi C arm, it has a bulge at the end with no bonds; however, there are still nucleotide positions. The part of the arm with bonds has the following colors: orange, orange, black, black, black. The bulge has a black dot and a purple dot on the left and two black dots on the right. At the very tip of the bulge is a yellow sequence labeled "anticodon." Its 3' end is on the right; its 5' end is on the left. It contains three red dots. Pointing to the left from the middle of the tRNA is the D arm. It also has a bulge at the end with no nucleotide bonds. The portion of the D arm that does have bonds has the following dot colors, from right to left: purple (which connects to a black dot), orange, black, black. The colors of the dots in the bulge are purple, black, black, black, purple, purple, blue, purple. (b) A complex 3-D image of the tRNA. The nucleotides are shown as flat colored polygons. Whatever colors are present on one strand are mirrored in the opposite strand. The color of the nucleotides corresponds to the color of the backbone, which is twisted into a helix and is shaped like an upside-down L. The amino acid arm is at the upper right; its 3' end is purple. Following the strand to the left, there is a blue section, then a short orange section, and another short blue section. After the blue section, the strand gives way to the large green region. The strands twist away from the reader in a half-twist. They separate briefly to form the T psi C arm, which has a long purple section, a short green section, another purple section, and a long orange section. The T psi C arm makes up the curve in the L shape. The 5' strand curves around the back of the molecule, where it has a short orange section, a green section, a purple section, another green section, a purple section, and a blue section. The blue section is on the left, after the 5' strand has curved around the back. The blue section is labeled the D arm. After the blue section, the 3' strand dips downward and to the right, and there is another purple section. The strand turns green again for a large stretch, then there is a downward twisting region that alternates orange and green. This is labeled the anticodon arm on the right. The helix twists downward and opens up slightly. At the bottom right is a yellow section with red nucleotides labeled "anticodon." To the bottom left of the anticodon is a short purple section.
